newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo port bans vessels below 3,000 tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Colombo port bans vessels below 3,000 tonnes.

text.p: The Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) on Wednesday, citing security reasons, banned the entry of vessels below 3,000 tonnes from entering the Colombo port.
"All vessels less than 3,000 tonnes, including those from (the south Indian port of) Tuticorin will be diverted to Galle with immediate effect," an SLPA spokesman said.
He said without elaborating that the restriction was imposed for security reasons. Sri Lankan troops are fighting a Tamil guerrilla insurgency since 1983 and ports are a rebel target.
Other port officials said the ban was requested by the navy because of fears that Tamil Tiger rebels might use the small vessels to attack Colombo port, a key South Asian transhipment centre.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels (LTTE), fighting for independence for minority Tamils in the north and east, staged an abortive suicide attack on the port in April this year.
In May last year, Colombo begun diverting vessels below 1,500 tonnes from Tuticorin to Sri Lanka's southern port of Galle for the same reasons, port and shipping agency officials said.
